# `union-kind-changed`

anyOf/oneOf kind changed

| | |
|---|---|
| **Kind** | `wire` |
| **Default severity** | `warn` in requests, `warn` in responses · `--profile sdk`: `error` |
| **Rule IDs** | `union-kind-changed` (both directions), `union-kind-changed-in-request`, `union-kind-changed-in-response` |
| **Status** | Implemented (M5) |
| **Group** | Schemas ([RULES.md section 7](../../RULES.md)) |

## What it detects

`anyOf` became `oneOf` or the other way round.

## Why this default

On the wire, values matching several branches change validity. In generated SDKs, union types change shape.

## Example

From test case [`union-kind-changed`](../../test/cases/union-kind-changed/): anyOf became oneOf.

`openapi.yaml`, base → revision:

```diff
  …
    schemas:
      Pet:
-       anyOf:
+       oneOf:
        - $ref: '#/components/schemas/Cat'
        - $ref: '#/components/schemas/Dog'
```

Findings:

- `union-kind-changed-in-response` · warn · #/components/schemas/Pet

## Policy options

Every rule takes `severity` (`error`, `warn`, `info` or `off`), `fix` and `explanation` in the policy file, for the generic ID or any variant ID above (the more specific ID wins). The policy file arrives in M6; see [POLICY.md](../../POLICY.md).

```yaml
rules:
  union-kind-changed: warn
```

## How to fix

Keep the original keyword.
